newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to begin reopening of Hebron thoroughfare.
newsitem.headline: Israel to begin reopening of Hebron thoroughfare.

text.p: Israel said on Friday it would begin to gradually reopen a main commerical thoroughfare in the West Bank city of Hebron to Palestinian vehicles next week.
"Next week the army intends to begin the gradual opening of Shuhada street in Hebron," an Israel army spokeswoman said.

Israel handed over 80 percent of Hebron to PLO rule on January 17 under a U.S.-brokered deal. Shuhada (Martyrs) street, which borders Jewish settlements, is in the 20 percent of the city under Israeli control.

The accord states that the street, closed to Palestinian vehicles since February 1994 when a Jewish settler from a nearby settlement massacred 29 Arabs kneeling in prayer at al-Ibrahimi mosque, will be gradually reopened within four months.
A Palestinian vegetable market is located on Shuhada street. Some 400 Jewish settlers, who opposed the handover, live in the heart of the volatile city, home to 100,000 Arabs.

"The army and the Palestinian Authority are discussing the issue of opening the street taking into consideration all the factors. It must be stressed that it is a gradual opening of the street," the spokeswoman said.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat told reporters in Gaza on Friday that he was insisting the Hebron deal be implemented, including the opening of Shuhada street.

"It was supposed to be directly and I am sorry to say that we are insisting to see an implementation, not a delay, for what has been agreed upon," Arafat, speaking in English, said when asked about Israel's decision to reopen the street.
